tasks.short: Match each application to the vacancy's hard requirements and record the result.

steps.what: Turn the vacancy into a confirmed checklist

loop.input: Vacancy text plus the role's certificate and pay-scale fields
loop.output: A checklist: certificate, site, shift, licence, language, right to work; anything else marked not a rule
loop.check: Each item is on the closed list or marked not a rule; the recruiter confirms the list once per vacancy
loop.stop: One pass. If an item is neither a list value nor marked not a rule, the vacancy is not published
loop.why_not_simpler: The requirements are still partly in prose. A fixed form can replace the loop once the fields exist

steps.what: Read the application into dossier fields

loop.input: The application the candidate submitted, including a photo of a certificate
loop.output: Name, vacancy, dates, certificate names, site and shift preference
loop.check: Vacancy id is present, dates parse, certificate names map to the catalogue or unknown. No BSN is stored
loop.stop: One retry. A failed check goes to the recruiter queue and is not scored
loop.why_not_simpler: Layouts vary, and many applications are themselves model-written prose. The fields are checkable; the prose is not

steps.what: Mark pass, fail, or needs a look
Draft a one-line reason that cites a field

loop.input: The knockout result and the dossier fields that fired
loop.output: One sentence naming the field, or no sentence
loop.check: Every claim cites a dossier field. No score. No age, health, origin, family or belief
loop.stop: If the check fails, the row stays needs a look, with no sentence
loop.why_not_simpler: The sentence is for the recruiter and the manager. A code alone is enough for the machine; people still ask why

steps.what: File the result on the candidate card

tasks.design: A checklist the recruiter confirms once per vacancy, fed by Recruitee, the AFAS pay scale and Studytube. A loop only reads the application into fields and, where the check passes, writes one sentence that cites a field. Rules mark pass, fail or needs a look. Nothing is rejected and nothing is sent to a manager until the recruiter accepts the pile. There is no match score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements lived in vacancy prose, certificates lived in Studytube, and a score was the product on offer. A score does not say which field fired, and the works council had no list to consent to.
tasks.enabler_now: The three systems have APIs. A short extraction loop is good enough when every field is checked against a catalogue. Writing the checklist is days of work once; the consent is the long part.
tasks.still_hard: Photos of certificates, unknown certificate names, and internal staff whose Studytube record is right and whose CV is thin. The needs-a-look pile does not shrink by wishing.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which site will take a near-miss, and which near-miss is a protected situation that a checklist must not decide.

ambition.what: Internal warehouse staff who hold a valid certificate in Studytube and have not applied.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter stops re-reading CVs for VCA, licence and site, and reviews the needs-a-look pile and the internal matches. They gain the right to confirm the checklist that later rejections must cite.

reach.task: Enrol a near-miss on the missing certificate
reach.learn: Which certificates Studytube can book before day one, so a gap becomes a course rather than a rejection.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 can build a profile from an application and calculate a match score. No accuracy figure is published, so this design does not use a score.
CV screening almost always needs works-council consent before use, and a decision without it can be nullified within a month.
A rejection may not rest solely on a score, and a review is not real if the person must follow the outcome.
A back-end ranker generally falls outside the Article 50 chatbot notice. Filtering applications is high-risk once the deferred duties apply.

assumptions: Hard requirements can be written as a closed list: certificate, site, shift, licence, language, right to work
Studytube is the source for certificates Noordhaven itself issued or recorded
Consent days sit in one works-council file shared with the other recruiting blocks, not a separate file per task
Hours are the O*NET share times 1,600, not a time study
unknowns: Whether any knockout rules are written down today
Applications per vacancy, and the share that arrive as a photo or a scan
Whether the works council has already consented to anything in Recruitee
Whether internal certificates in Studytube cover agency-trained people or only employees
research_questions: For the last twenty hires, which requirement, if missing, would have made the person unable to start?
How many applications last quarter were rejected, and is the reason in Recruitee or only in a mailbox?

tasks.short: Tell applicants the duties, pay, shifts and conditions of the role.

steps.what: Build the vacancy fact pack from source fields
Publish the pack and the acknowledgement
Answer a repeated question with an approved snippet

loop.input: The candidate's question and the vacancy fact pack
loop.output: A snippet id whose numbers equal the pack, or not in the pack
loop.check: The snippet exists and every figure in it equals the pack. Otherwise not in the pack
loop.stop: One pass. Not in the pack goes to the recruiter. No free answer is sent
loop.why_not_simpler: The question is free text. The answer is not: it may only be a sentence already approved

steps.what: Draft an answer the pack does not cover

loop.output: A draft that quotes the pack or asks the recruiter for the missing fact
loop.check: No pay figure appears that is not in the pack
loop.stop: One draft. The recruiter sends or rewrites. The draft never sends itself
loop.why_not_simpler: The missing fact is not on the checklist, so a snippet cannot exist yet

steps.what: Explain a personal situation to the applicant

tasks.design: Pay scale, allowances, shift, site and certificates are fields, assembled into a vacancy fact pack and published with the vacancy. Repeated questions are classified onto snippets whose figures must equal the pack. Anything else is a draft the recruiter sends. A personal situation stays a conversation. This is not a candidate chatbot.
tasks.previous_blocker: The facts were in three places, so every answer was retyped, and a wrong scale was easy to send.
tasks.enabler_now: The pack is the same object as the checklist. Snippets are configuration. A classifier is only there to refuse questions the pack does not cover.
tasks.still_hard: A candidate comparing two shifts, or asking for an adjustment, is not a snippet. Shift premiums that are not in AFAS as a field will keep producing drafts.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that the question about the shift is really a question about care, travel or health, and answering without putting that into a template.

ambition.what: State scale, shift and certificates on every vacancy before it is published, including flex orders.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter stops restating the CAO scale in mail. They keep the conversations where the pack is silent, and they own the snippets, so a wrong figure is a field to fix.

reach.task: Keep the scale and allowance fields that the pack quotes
reach.learn: Which CAO components are fields in AFAS and which are still a PDF on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: An ordinary job ad or candidate email that a recruiter has substantively reviewed usually needs no Article 50 label. A chatbot that talks to the candidate does, at the first turn.

assumptions: Stock acknowledgement and snippets are approved once by a recruiter, so each send of an exact snippet has no further person in the loop
Noordhaven's Recruitee tenant can send a stage or acknowledgement message. No Recruitee product page was opened for this run
Wrong pay in a mail is the expensive error, so the pack is the only allowed source of figures
unknowns: Whether stage and acknowledgement mail is already switched on
Which allowance and shift-premium figures are fields, and which are only in the CAO PDF
How many candidate questions a week are pay, shift, or something else
research_questions: Take twenty candidate mails from last month: how many are answered by the pack alone?
Is the published pay band the same figure AFAS would put on the contract?

tasks.short: Choose who to refer to a manager and record the recommendation.

steps.what: Assemble the shortlist pack from prior steps
Draft the recommendation from the pack

loop.output: A memo in which each sentence cites a pack field, and gaps stay gaps
loop.check: No sentence without a field. No score. No comparison the pack does not contain
loop.stop: One draft. If the check fails, the recruiter writes the memo with no draft
loop.why_not_simpler: The pack is structured. The memo is what the manager will read, and managers do not read field dumps

steps.what: Decide who to refer and talk to the manager
Log the decision and the reason code
Hand the outcome to the status message

tasks.design: The shortlist pack is assembled from the knockout, the certificate check and the scorecard. A loop may draft the memo only from those fields. The recruiter decides who is referred and talks to the manager. The manager's decision is logged as a reason code before any status mail is released. The same pack is not built again in the matching task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The recommendation was a fresh document each time, so the reason lived in mail and the decision record was thin.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the pack exists, the memo is a view of it. The decision itself is unchanged and stays with people.
tasks.still_hard: Two adequate people and one job. The pack does not make that choice, and it should not pretend to.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a manager why a needs-a-look candidate is worth an hour, including context a field will not hold.

ambition.what: Refer a complete pack the day the checklist closes, instead of holding names for a weekly meeting.

tasks.altitude: Less time assembling paper, the same weight on the referral. The recruiter gains a decision record that HR admin can open, and does not gain the right to hire.

reach.task: Open the contract pack the day the decision is logged
reach.learn: Which AFAS fields the contract needs, so week-one onboarding is not a second round of questions.

evidence.claim: Hiring leaders report wide use of screening tools, and 26 percent fear they no longer see some candidates. The needs-a-look pile is kept visible because of that.
The employer remains responsible for the hiring tool. A contract does not decide whether a statute applies.

assumptions: The hiring manager, not the recruiter, makes the hire decision
Hours saved on the pack are counted once, on the matching task's checklist and here only as assembly
A reason code list already exists or can be agreed with the HR director
unknowns: Who may hire today: recruiter, HR business partner, or the site manager
Whether internal candidates follow the same stages
How often a referral waits for a weekly meeting rather than a decision
research_questions: Last quarter, what was the median number of days from a complete checklist to the manager's yes or no?
Where is the reason written today when someone is not referred?

tasks.short: Schedule certificate checks and trials, and file the pass or fail.

steps.what: Read which certificate or trial the role needs
Check Studytube for a certificate still in date
Offer a slot and send the invite
Reschedule a no-show
File the structured pass or fail flag
Decide whether a fail stops the hire

tasks.design: The role catalogue says which certificate or practical trial is required. Studytube answers validity with a date compare. Slots are offered from a calendar and a person approves the invite. A pass or fail flag can be filed. A medical, drug or psychological narrative is stored as a restricted document and is never passed to a model. The stop-or-continue decision stays with a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: The class says the task is human, so the booking and the chasing were left in the mailbox. The sensitive file and the diary were treated as one problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Validity is a date. Booking is a calendar. The sensitive document can be kept out of the loop by never giving the loop the file.
tasks.still_hard: A provider who only sends a PDF letter, a no-show on a night-shift trial, and any result that is not a clean pass or fail. Drug and medical tests are lawful only in narrow cases; this design does not decide that.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a borderline practical trial, and refusing to treat a health document as a score.

ambition.what: Night-shift candidates who currently wait until the next office day for a slot.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter books and files instead of hunting certificates across Studytube and inboxes. They do not gain the right to interpret a medical result.

reach.task: Book the course when the certificate is missing but the person is otherwise through
reach.learn: Lead time on forklift, VCA and food-safety courses at each site.

evidence.claim: Inferring emotion from face or voice in recruitment is already prohibited. A video trial must not be used that way.
Scheduling is one of the three uses US hiring leaders most often name. That is self-reported use, not a Noordhaven time study.
Health and drug-test documents are special-category data and should not be sent to a model. This is model knowledge of GDPR practice, not a page opened for this run.

assumptions: Most of this task at Noordhaven is certificates and practical trials, not intelligence or personality tests
A structured pass or fail is available for practical trials. Medical letters are the exception and stay manual
The catalogue of requirements is the same object as in the test-design task
unknowns: Which roles require a medical, a drug test, or a VOG
Who the assessors are at each site, and whether their calendar is bookable
Whether any current test uses a vendor score the recruiter does not see
research_questions: Which roles started someone last year without the certificate the catalogue now says is required?
How many results last quarter arrived as a PDF letter rather than a yes or no?

tasks.short: Tell applicants where their application stands.

steps.what: Detect a stage change or fourteen quiet days
Send the stock message for that stage
Send a rejection tied to a reason code
Answer a status question from the stage clock

loop.input: The candidate's question and that candidate's stage clock row
loop.output: A reply that states the stage name and the date, or not a status question
loop.check: The reply contains only the stage and the date. No other candidate is mentioned
loop.stop: One pass. Anything else goes to the recruiter unsent
loop.why_not_simpler: The question is free text. The allowed answer is one row of the clock

steps.what: Handle an offer, a complaint, or an internal candidate

tasks.design: Recruitee stage changes, and a fourteen-day silence, write a stage clock. Stock messages go out from templates a recruiter has approved. A rejection is a reason code the recruiter releases, not a generated letter. Offers, complaints and internal candidates stay manual. The clock is the same list the weekly plan uses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status lived in memory and in the mailbox. Silence had no row, so only the candidates who chased got an answer.
tasks.enabler_now: Stage is already a field. Counting days is code. The fourteen-day figure is a parameter, taken from a published pile-up, not a claim that Noordhaven will match anyone else's result.
tasks.still_hard: A rejection that needs a human explanation beyond the code, and any message about an offer. Templates rot when the stage list changes.
tasks.human_edge: Writing to someone who was close, or who is already an employee, without hiding behind a template.

ambition.what: Tell every applicant the stage when fourteen days have passed, not only the ones who write in.

tasks.altitude: The morning starts with the quiet rows, not with the inbox. The recruiter can nudge a manager because the row is dated, and still owns every rejection.

reach.task: See which site managers are the bottleneck on open roles
reach.learn: How to read days-in-stage without turning it into a league table of managers.

evidence.claim: Uniper's hiring agent, given process context, named 27 candidates shortlisted more than 14 days. Time to contract signature fell 27 days and the screening phase 13 days. No baseline duration was published, and the figures come from the company and its vendors.
A recruiter-reviewed email usually needs no Article 50 label. Spell-check is not that review.

assumptions: Fourteen days is the default parameter because it is the published example, and Noordhaven can change it
Stock templates are approved in substance by a recruiter before they are switched on
This task owns the stage clock. Strategy and criteria read it and do not rebuild it
unknowns: Current median days by stage
Whether candidates already receive automatic stage mail
How many status chases a week arrive by phone rather than mail
research_questions: What share of open applications have had no stage change for more than fourteen days?
Which rejections last quarter have a reason code, and which are only a sentence in Outlook?

tasks.short: Find people for open roles from internal pools, agencies and outreach.

steps.what: Search staff and past applicants by certificate and site
Match an agency bench file to the order

loop.input: The agency's mail or CSV of names
loop.check: Each certificate maps to the catalogue or is missing. Names are checked for a duplicate in AFAS
loop.stop: One retry, then the file sits in the queue unmatched
loop.why_not_simpler: The company profile gives email and CSV, not an agency API. The columns will not be stable

steps.what: Draft an outreach note for the recruiter to send

loop.input: The vacancy fact pack and the person's name and certificate
loop.output: A short note a recruiter can send, naming Noordhaven and the role
loop.check: It names the employer and the role, makes no match-score claim, and adds no fact that is not in the pack
loop.stop: One draft. Unsent if the check fails. It does not contact anyone
loop.why_not_simpler: A template covers the standard note. The loop is only for a note that has to mention a specific certificate or site

steps.what: Choose who to approach and send the note
Meet people at fairs and follow up referrals

tasks.design: Search starts inside the house: employees, Studytube certificates, and past applicants who already passed a checklist. Agency benches are read from the file they actually send. Outreach is a draft the recruiter sends. There is no sourcing agent and no job-board API in this stack. Fairs and referrals stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: External tools were the picture of search. Noordhaven's reachable data is AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and three inboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: The checklist and the agency order exist as records, so internal search and bench matching are joins. A person still decides who is contacted.
tasks.still_hard: People who asked not to be contacted, name collisions, and agency files that change shape. Job boards remain a screen. Rules cover under half of the choice of who to approach, and that choice stays.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who in the region will pick up, and who would resent a second approach.

ambition.what: Past applicants who passed the checklist and were not hired, before any new outreach.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter spends the search hour on people, not on retyping a bench file. They keep the decision of who is approached. They do not get an agent that writes to strangers overnight.

reach.task: Flag internal people who are ready to move site
reach.learn: How a move interacts with the CAO and with the person's current roster.

evidence.claim: Workday's talent acquisition agent can draft outreach, and the release says the outreach is not sent until a recruiter approves it. Early access from October 2026; general availability planned for early 2027. Noordhaven does not run Workday.
An outbound sourcing agent must say it is AI and name who it acts for. This design avoids that by keeping the send with the recruiter.
71 percent of surveyed US hiring leaders believed most applications they screened were model-written. More paper is not a better pool.

assumptions: No sourcing-tool API is in the company stack. LinkedIn and job boards stay manual
Searching employees by certificate is allowed once the works council has seen the purpose
The bench file is the same object the agency-order task produces
unknowns: Whether past applicants have been told their data may be reused for a later role
How the three agencies deliver names today: CSV, PDF, or a portal screen
Whether a do-not-contact flag exists anywhere
research_questions: Of hires last year, how many were internal, how many from the three agencies, how many from a job board?
Is there a retention difference at 90 days by those sources, or is the field empty?

tasks.short: Run reference and background checks and decide if they clear.

steps.what: Open a check when the role and stage require it
Send the candidate a consent form
Request the reference or VOG after consent returns
Send one reminder, then stop
Extract dates and role; flag adverse words

loop.output: Dates, role, and would-rehire if stated; otherwise not stated. Adverse sentences flagged, not interpreted
loop.check: Each extracted value is a quote or not stated. The loop does not recommend hire or reject
loop.stop: One pass. A reply that is not a reference goes to the recruiter whole
loop.why_not_simpler: Replies are free text. The decision is not extractable, and must not be generated

steps.what: Decide whether the check clears the hire

tasks.design: The stage and the role open a check. Consent goes out first, and no referee is contacted without that file. One reminder, then a person. A loop may quote dates and role from the reply and flag adverse lines. It does not clear anyone. A VOG or a narrative reference is decided by the recruiter with the HR director when the finding is adverse.
tasks.previous_blocker: Chasing paper was mixed up with the judgement, and both stayed in the mailbox. Consent was a sentence in a mail rather than a file the request checks for.
tasks.enabler_now: The request is a checklist: role needs it, consent is present, one reminder, then stop. Extraction is safe only because it is forbidden to conclude.
tasks.still_hard: A referee who phones instead of writing, a VOG that needs a judgement, and the long tail of people who do not reply. Adverse findings are rare and expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a careful negative reference, and deciding what it means for this role rather than for a score.
tasks.altitude: The chase shortens. The clear-or-not decision does not move. Nothing in the week should make checks more automatic when the finding is bad.

reach.task: File the VOG or reference on the employee record after the yes
reach.learn: Which document types AFAS restricts, and who may open them.

evidence.claim: A profile built from data beyond the application is the allegation in the Eightfold case. This check uses only what the candidate consented to release.
VOG (certificate of conduct) applies to some Dutch roles and not others. Which Noordhaven roles need one is unknown. Model knowledge.

assumptions: No reference request leaves without a stored consent
The loop is not allowed to recommend
Criminal-record information is special and is not put in the stage clock
unknowns: Which roles require a VOG, a reference, both, or neither
Who may see an adverse result
How often referees reply by phone
research_questions: For which roles did Noordhaven request a VOG or a reference in the last year?
How many offers were waiting on a check for more than ten days?

tasks.short: Interview applicants and write a scorecard the manager can use.

steps.what: Draft questions from the skill list and the bank

loop.input: The skills on the vacancy and the approved question bank
loop.output: Two questions per skill, each tied to a skill id
loop.check: Every question maps to a skill. The recruiter deletes any that ask about health, family, origin or belief
loop.stop: One draft. If the bank has no question for a skill, the kit says so and does not invent a test
loop.why_not_simpler: The bank covers known skills. A new skill has no approved question until a person writes one

steps.what: Book the manager and send the kit
Interview the candidate
Write the scorecard on the form
File the scorecard on the candidate

tasks.design: A question bank plus the vacancy's skills produces a kit the recruiter edits. The interview stays a conversation, on site or on Teams, with no recording and no generated summary. The recruiter writes the scorecard on a form. The form is configuration. The words are the person's. The kit's coverage is not evidence that hires get better.
tasks.previous_blocker: Managers reused generic questions, and a transcript looked like a way to save the write-up. The transcript then becomes the record managers trust.
tasks.enabler_now: A question tied to a skill is a template. Writing it for a known bank is a draft with a check. That does not touch the hour in the room.
tasks.still_hard: The interview itself, about half this task. A stand-in manager who has not done it before. Any pressure to record so the summary can be skimmed.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing whether the person can do the shift and the work, and noticing an unlawful question before it is asked.

ambition.what: Give every hiring manager, including a stand-in, a skill-tied question set instead of generic questions on the day.

tasks.altitude: The interview week does not shrink much. Preparation does. The recruiter keeps the scorecard pen, which is the point: the note is theirs, not a model's.

reach.task: Coach a manager whose scorecards are empty or unlawful
reach.learn: Which questions the works council and the CAO will not accept.

evidence.claim: Workday's own team generated questions for more than 800 skills across 1,600 roles. There is no evidence in that account that the questions produced better hires.
Interview summaries become the record managers read. Notetakers err, drop context, and can store an unlawful question.
Emotion inference from face or voice in recruitment is prohibited.

assumptions: Noordhaven will not record interviews for a generated summary
A question bank can be written for warehouse and office roles without a vendor
The scorecard is the same object the shortlist pack reads
unknowns: Whether Teams transcription is already on by default
Who interviews warehouse roles: recruiter, site lead, or both
Whether a scorecard exists today or the note is a mail
research_questions: Do hiring managers see the candidate before they see a written summary?
Which skills on the ten most common roles have no agreed question?

tasks.short: Check whether selection criteria still meet standards, and propose changes.

steps.what: Build the 90-day outcome table by criterion and site
Flag small samples and sharp site gaps
Draft a change to one criterion

loop.input: The outcome table and the small-sample flags
loop.output: A proposed change that quotes the cells it uses
loop.check: Every number in the draft is a cell in the table. A small-sample flag forces the sentence do not conclude
loop.stop: One draft. The HR director decides. No criterion changes itself
loop.why_not_simpler: The table is deterministic. The sentence that proposes a change is what the meeting will argue about

steps.what: Decide the change with the HR director

tasks.design: A Power BI page joins the stage clock, the decision record and AFAS at day 90, by criterion and site. Rules flag samples the HR director has called too small, and gaps between sites. A loop may draft one change and must quote the cells. The director decides, and the works council is in the room if the change alters screening. The same table serves the test-design task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outcomes were not joined to criteria, so the review was a feeling after a bad hire. Small numbers invite a confident wrong conclusion.
tasks.enabler_now: Day-90 employment is an AFAS fact. Stage days are the clock. The join is ordinary. The discipline is to print do not conclude when the count is thin.
tasks.still_hard: Flex workers may not be in the 90-day field. Three sites and seasonal peaks make many slices too small. A criterion can be legal and still a bad predictor, or a good predictor and still unlawful.
tasks.human_edge: Refusing a tidy story the table does not support, and knowing when a difference is a site practice rather than a criterion.

ambition.what: Review 90-day retention by criterion twice a year, not only after a complaint.

tasks.altitude: Twice a year the recruiter walks in with a table instead of a stack of CVs. They do not gain the right to change a criterion alone.

reach.task: Own the join between Recruitee hires and AFAS day-90
reach.learn: Which hire is payroll, which is flex, and which 90-day definition the North Star uses.

evidence.claim: The Dutch data-protection authority finds recruitment AI weak on explainability. A criterion change has to be explainable in the table, not as a score.
Filtering and evaluating candidates are high-risk uses. The deployer duties, including informing workers' representatives, are deferred to 2 December 2027.
Under 5 percent of companies in a cited ManpowerGroup survey saw transformational results from AI hiring tools. A dashboard of criteria is not a better hire by itself.

assumptions: The HR director sets the small-sample threshold. This design does not invent one
90-day retention is the North Star's outcome, and it is stored for payroll hires
Hours for building the table are shared with the test-design task and are not two projects
unknowns: Whether 90-day retention is recorded for flex workers
How many hires a year per role and site, which decides whether any slice is large enough
Whether adverse-impact checks have ever been run
research_questions: Can AFAS answer, for last year's hires, who was still employed at day 90, by source and site?
What would the HR director treat as too small a sample to change a criterion?

tasks.short: Set the recruiting plan for the roles the sites actually need.

steps.what: Publish the weekly pipeline snapshot
Draft a one-page plan from that snapshot

loop.output: A page naming stuck roles and a next channel, with no target the snapshot cannot measure
loop.check: Every role named is a row on the snapshot. No target is invented
loop.stop: One draft. The meeting can ignore it
loop.why_not_simpler: The snapshot is the facts. The page is so the meeting starts from a sentence rather than a chart

steps.what: Agree the plan with the director and the sites
Turn agreed actions into vacancies and orders

tasks.design: The weekly picture is the stage clock plus agency fill, not a new agent. A loop may draft one page from that picture. The HR director and the sites agree the plan in a meeting. Agreed actions become vacancies and agency orders. The plan is judged later, at day 90, which is why most of the checking cannot be done up front.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was a quarterly slide, disconnected from who was stuck this week. The probe calls the task a workflow. The work is a meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The clock already names quiet stages. Writing the page is a draft with a check that it cannot invent a role or a target.
tasks.still_hard: Site leads who disagree about whether a role is open, and a seasonal spike that makes last month's plan stale. The effect of the plan is only visible later.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing where to spend a scarce week: a hard warehouse role, a fair, or a manager who will not move.

ambition.what: Name the stuck roles with the sites every week, not in a quarterly slide.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter walks into the weekly meeting with rows, and leaves with orders. They gain a regular decision on where effort goes. They do not gain a plan that executes itself.

reach.task: Choose which open roles are worth a fair or a retained search
reach.learn: What a fair and an agency actually cost, from finance, so the choice is not only in hours.

evidence.claim: On raw HR data, Uniper's agent gave generalities. With process context it named a specific pile-up. The snapshot here is that context, built as a query, not as an agent.
Workday's release says time to fill moves from weeks to days. That is a slogan in a vendor announcement, not a customer result, and it is not used as a target.

assumptions: The snapshot reuses the stage clock. Its build days are marginal
A weekly meeting with sites either exists or the HR director will start one. The tool does not create the meeting
Strategy hours are not added on top of the status-task savings
unknowns: Whether a pipeline meeting already happens
Who is allowed to open a vacancy
How far ahead sites know their seasonal peak
research_questions: Which open roles this week have had no stage change, and who is the waiting party?
Did last year's recruiting plan name a channel per role, or only a headcount?

tasks.short: Order flex workers from agencies and check the names that come back.

steps.what: Take the site order on a form
Check the pay-scale fields are filled
Send the order to the agency
Match returned names to certificates and AFAS

loop.input: The agency's returned names in mail or CSV
loop.output: Name, certificate in date or fail, duplicate in AFAS or not
loop.check: Certificate maps to the catalogue and the date, or the row is fail. No score
loop.stop: One retry. A file that fails the check is not partly accepted
loop.why_not_simpler: There is no agency API in the company profile. The loop only reads the file the rule then judges

steps.what: Call the agency when the fill or the rate fails
Confirm the start to the site and HR admin

tasks.design: The site lead submits a form: role, shift, headcount, start, certificates. Rules refuse an order whose pay fields are empty, using the inlenersbeloning terms as fields, not as a paragraph. The recruiter approves the send. Returned names are read from mail or CSV and matched to certificates and to AFAS. A fail is refused only after the recruiter confirms. The Monday phone call stays a call.
tasks.previous_blocker: Three agencies, no API, and the order lived in mail. The O*NET frequency says more than yearly, which hid a weekly mess. The class says human, which hid the form.
tasks.enabler_now: The order is a record. Certificate validity is a date. The phone call is the residue, and it is smaller than the retyping.
tasks.still_hard: A Monday morning when nobody qualified is available, a rate dispute, and a name who worked here before under another spelling. Portals that only offer a screen will keep a person in the loop.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which agency will actually fill Tilburg nights, and when to tell the site the order is short rather than pretend.

ambition.what: Night-shift leads, who can submit an order without waiting for the office to read a mailbox.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter reviews exceptions and makes the calls. They gain the right to refuse a name that fails a confirmed certificate or an empty pay field. They do not gain the right to change the rate.

reach.task: Register the flex start without retyping the order
reach.learn: Which AFAS fields a flex start needs, and which the agency is allowed to see.

evidence.claim: Hirers of agency workers in the Netherlands have to apply the client's pay terms (inlenersbeloning). The field check is that duty turned into required fields. Model knowledge; no statute page was opened for this run.
An arrangement that processes personnel data generally needs works-council consent before use.

assumptions: The 157 team hours are the O*NET share. They were not increased to match 150 to 300 flex workers
Inlenersbeloning can be expressed as fields the compensation specialist maintains
A data-processing arrangement with each agency exists or will be signed before names flow
unknowns: How many flex orders a week, by site and season
Whether the three agencies will send a stable CSV
What a missed Monday shift costs. Not estimated here
research_questions: How many agency orders went out last month, and how many names failed a certificate or a pay field?
Are the inlenersbeloning components already fields in AFAS?

tasks.short: Keep the test catalogue and judge whether each test earns its place.

steps.what: Maintain the requirement catalogue per role
Write the assessor brief from the catalogue
Add the test's pass rate to the outcome table
Judge whether the test is fair and useful
Draft the keep, drop, or change recommendation

loop.input: The outcome table, including the small-sample flag from the criteria review
loop.output: A keep, drop, or change note that cites the count
loop.check: The note cites the count. If the small-sample flag is set, the only allowed recommendation is do not conclude
loop.stop: One draft. No test is switched off by the draft
loop.why_not_simpler: The counts are rules. The recommendation is a sentence the director will sign

tasks.design: This task keeps the catalogue of what each role requires and the one-page brief an assessor uses. Pass rates land on the same outcome table as the criteria review. Scheduling stays in the scheduling task and is not rebuilt. Judging whether a test is fair stays a meeting. A draft recommendation may not outrun a small sample.
tasks.previous_blocker: Develop, administer and evaluate were one O*NET line, so a build would have cloned the scheduler and the dashboard. The sensitive part is the judgement, which is a small share.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalogue is a list. The brief is a template. The table is already specified on the criteria task.
tasks.still_hard: A new practical test that has to be fair across three sites, and any proposal to add a psychological test. That is a different legal object and is out of this design.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a test which predicts staying is still the wrong test, because of what it asks or who it drops.
tasks.altitude: The catalogue stops being a PDF nobody updates. The judgement of a test stays a meeting with the director. The job does not become test design as a profession unless the person trains for it.

reach.task: Retire a certificate requirement that the table cannot support
reach.learn: What a defensible practical trial looks like, and when to call in a specialist rather than invent one.

evidence.claim: Changing how candidates are evaluated is the high-risk recruitment use. Duties are deferred to 2 December 2027 and include informing workers' representatives. Existing systems are caught when significantly changed.
A works-council consent gap can be invoked within one month. Changing the catalogue is a selection arrangement, not a private edit.

assumptions: Noordhaven's tests are certificates and practical trials. This task does not add psychometric products
Pass-rate reporting reuses the criteria table. Build days are the catalogue and the brief only
The recruiter prepares the recommendation. The HR director decides
unknowns: Whether any test in use today was validated, and by whom
Pass rates by site for the practical trials
Whether assessors use the same brief
research_questions: List every test or certificate now required, by role. Which have a written brief?
For the practical trial used most often, what is the pass rate by site over the last year?

role.altitude: The two recruiters start the day on the stage clock: who has been quiet for fourteen days, which agency name failed a rule, which needs-a-look pile is waiting. The rest of the week is interviews, the referral conversation, and the agency call when a fill fails. They gain the right to release a rejection that cites a confirmed field, to refuse an agency name that fails one, and to put a stuck role in front of a manager with a date. They do not gain the right to hire, to score, or to read a medical file. The job stays expert on three sites and gets less expert at retyping.
reach: HR admin can open the contract the day the decision is logged, if the recruiter learns which AFAS fields that pack needs.
Learning and development can enrol a near-miss before day one, if the recruiter learns which certificates are bookable at each site.
The people analyst can use the same 90-day table, if the recruiter learns which starts are payroll and which are flex.
The HR business partner can see which managers hold a stage, if the recruiter learns to show days without making a league table.
skills_to_grow: Write a knockout list the works council can read, with each item either a field or not a rule
Read a 90-day table, including when the count is too small to change anything
Know which roles need a VOG, and which pay fields inlenersbeloning requires on an agency order
role.ambitious_version: Each morning the stuck stages are named, and a night-shift lead can place a flex order that is checked before the recruiter starts. That is a decision made every day, and a group served that currently waits for the office. The season swings the volume, so the order form has to cope with a quiet week and a peak week. It is not a plan to do the interview for every applicant by machine.
